pure-announcement.rationale: An evergreen, comprehensive security reference doc that has existed for years, not a launch or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: Nearest concepts address different specific mechanisms in the same broad domain — exposure-first-supply-chain-defense is about credential theft via install hooks and long-lived tokens, unsandboxed-extension-marketplace-defenses is about marketplace-side scanning for open submission — neither covers pinning consumption to an immutable content hash versus trusting a mutable, repointable reference.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Official first-party GitHub documentation with a concrete, independently verifiable mechanism (SHA-1 collision resistance) and links to real enforcement policy configuration.

durability.rationale: Pinning to an immutable content hash instead of trusting a mutable, repointable reference is a foundational supply-chain practice that predates and outlives GitHub Actions specifically (the same principle underlies Docker image digests, Go's go.sum, Nix's content-addressed store) — a mechanism, not a version number.

actionability.rationale: Gives a directly adoptable practice — pin to full commit SHA, verify it against the real upstream repo not a fork, enforce it via repo/org policy — that changes exactly how someone would configure a CI pipeline or any registry-consumption workflow.

atomicity.rationale: The full note is a comprehensive security reference bundling many unrelated topics — secrets handling, script-injection mitigation, untrusted checkout risk, CODEOWNERS, OpenID Connect, Dependabot updates, self-hosted runner hardening, vulnerability screening — of which SHA-pinning against mutable references is only one section among many separable ideas.
